lines.say: Athletic scholarships are only about two percent of college grant money.

lines.text: The myth: scholarships are only for straight-A students and athletes. Here's the money.

lines.text: In 2024-25, students got $173.7 billion in grants.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-four to twenty-five, students got about one hundred seventy-four billion in grants.

lines.text: Colleges' own grants were $85.1 billion. NCAA athletic scholarships, $4 billion-plus.
lines.say: Colleges' own grants were about eighty-five billion. NCAA athletic scholarships, a bit over four billion.

lines.text: In 2025-26, 61% of students got a scholarship, averaging $8,291.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five to twenty-six, sixty-one percent of students got a scholarship, averaging about eighty-three hundred.

lines.text: Much of it is need-based, and many colleges use the FAFSA to award it.
lines.say: Much of it is need-based, and many colleges use the FAFSA to award it.

lines.text: NCAN estimates the class of 2024 left $4.4 billion in Pell Grants unclaimed.
lines.say: NCAN estimates the class of twenty twenty-four left about four point four billion in Pell Grants unclaimed.

lines.text: Max Pell for 2026-27: $7,395. Our math: 4 years, $29,580.
lines.say: Max Pell for twenty twenty-six to twenty-seven: seven thousand three hundred ninety-five dollars. Our math: four years, about twenty-nine thousand six hundred.

lines.text: Filing the FAFSA unlocks federal, state and many college grants.

post.title: Scholarships aren't just for straight-A students or athletes
post.ig:
Athletic scholarships are only about 2% of college grant money.
In 2024-25, students got $173.7B in grant aid; $85.1B came from colleges themselves.
The NCAA says athletic scholarships total $4B+ a year.
In 2025-26, 61% of students got a scholarship, averaging $8,291.
NCAN estimates the class of 2024 left $4.4B in Pell Grants unclaimed by not filing the FAFSA.
Sources: College Board Trends in Student Aid 2025, NCAA, Sallie Mae How America Pays for College 2026, NCAN, U.S. Dept. of Education.
News and education, not financial advice.
